key_insight: At late times, flow matching follows the geometry of the training set, approaching explicit paths that contract exponentially toward the nearest sample.
engineering_relevance: This geometry motivates simpler training targets and diagnostics that distinguish sample proximity, endpoint allocation, and feature fidelity.
method: Analyze linear-interpolation flow matching between independent Gaussian and empirical samples using the squared-distance potential.
Approximate late-time trajectories by explicit nearest-sample contraction paths away from Voronoi interfaces.
Learn either the distance potential with value-and-gradient supervision or velocities along contraction paths.
evidence_signal: Theoretical bounds establish a uniform-in-time square-root Wasserstein rate under specified restart laws, a two-site example shows sharpness in general, and MNIST experiments illustrate distinct evaluation criteria.
watch_item: Near Voronoi interfaces, nearest-sample assignments are ambiguous, and restart mass near these boundaries controls distributional approximation error.
paper_title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
